messages.content: Write the engineering culture section of a careers page. Around 250 words.

**Engineering culture**

We ship small. Most changes here go out the same week they're written, and if your pull request is 900 lines someone will ask — kindly — what the first 200 could have been on their own.

Code review is not a formality. Every change gets read by a person who doesn't share your assumptions about the service, and that person is expected to say so when something reads wrong. Disagreements go in the thread, not the hallway. We'd rather argue in writing where the next engineer can find it two years later.

You'll own things end to end: the design doc, the migration, the pager. That last part is real. Engineers here are on call for what they build, which keeps everyone honest about retries, timeouts, and the 3 a.m. cost of a clever abstraction. On-call is [X] days a quarter and we staff it so it's boring most weeks.

We write a lot. Design docs before big work, postmortems after incidents, no blame in either. When something breaks we want the mechanism, not a name.

What we don't do: heroics as a habit, planning theater, or rewriting a working system because it's five years old and someone read a blog post.

Most of our engineers came from somewhere they were not trusted to make decisions. We hire people who've been burned by that and want the opposite — a small team, a clear problem, and the room to be wrong in public and fix it fast.

---

The bracketed `[X]` is the one number I couldn't invent honestly — swap in your real on-call rotation, and adjust the "same week" ship cadence and PR-size line if they overstate your actual practice.

The text above has these problems. Rewrite it so none remain.
Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.

- colon_reveal (You'll own things end to end:):
- colon_reveal (What we don't do:):
- bold_density:
- thematic_break:
- paragraph_uniformity (7 paragraphs, spread 0.33):

Return only the rewritten text.
